objectives.statement: Understand foundational computer programming concepts, Python runtime architecture, and compilation vs. interpretation.
Master Python data types, literals, variables, arithmetic operators, operator precedence, and basic input/output operations.
Implement decision-making control flow, conditional execution, while/for loops, bitwise operations, and list manipulation.
Construct modular code using functions, variable scoping, immutable tuples, dictionaries, and defensive exception handling.

prerequisites: Basic computer literacy and ability to run commands in a terminal
Fundamental algebraic thinking (variables, arithmetic operations, logical conditions)

modules.title: Module 1: Introduction to Python and Computer Programming
modules.summary: Orient yourself with Cisco NetAcad's Python Essentials 1, understand computer architecture, machine vs. programming languages, compilation vs. interpretation, and write your first Python program with print().
lessonTitles: 1.3. The First Program & The print() Function
1.4. Practice Lab: print() Formatting & Escape Sequences
modules.checkpoint: Pass Module 1 Quiz (70%+), explain CPython execution steps, and correctly format formatted output.

modules.title: Module 2: Python Data Types, Variables, Operators, and Basic I/O Operations
modules.summary: Dive deep into Python literals (integers, floats, scientific notation, strings, booleans), arithmetic operators, operator precedence, variables, naming standards, comments, and the input() function.
lessonTitles: 2.5. User Interaction with input() & Type Casting
2.6. Module 2 Summary, Math Labs & Section Examination
modules.checkpoint: Complete the Pythagorean hypotenuse lab and score 70%+ on Module 2 operators and data types assessment.

modules.title: Module 3: Boolean Values, Conditional Execution, Loops, Lists and Logical Operations
modules.summary: Master conditional decision-making (if-elif-else), while and for loop control flow, boolean logic, bitwise operators, and mutable list operations including slicing and the Bubble Sort algorithm.
lessonTitles: 3.2. Loops in Python: while and for
3.6. Module 3 Summary, Classic Games Labs & Section Examination
modules.checkpoint: Implement Collatz hypothesis validator and pass the 20-question Module 3 logic assessment.

modules.title: Module 4: Functions, Tuples, Dictionaries, Exceptions, and Data Processing
modules.summary: Learn how to decompose complex problems into modular functions, handle variable scope, work with immutable tuples and key-value dictionaries, and safeguard code with defensive try-except blocks.
lessonTitles: 4.7. Module 4 NetAcad Capstone Project & Certification Exam
modules.checkpoint: Complete the Tic-Tac-Toe console game against AI and pass the 100-mark Cisco NetAcad Python Essentials 1 certification mock exam.

practiceActivities: Interactive terminal code evaluation for every chapter topic
Automated unit testing on hands-on NetAcad practice labs
Pythagorean distance, Collatz conjecture, and Bubble sort implementations
Defensive exception handling for input validation in production services
assessmentCheckpoints: Module 1 Section Assessment: Fundamentals and print() mechanics
Module 2 Section Assessment: Operators, type casting, and variable scoping
Module 3 Section Assessment: Branching decisions, loops, and list algorithms
Module 4 Section Assessment: Modular functions, dictionaries, and error handling
Comprehensive 100-Mark Timed Final Examination (28 authoritative questions)
projects: Cisco NetAcad Python Essentials 1 Capstone: Interactive AI Tic-Tac-Toe Console Game with modular functions, board representation, win-condition matrix validation, and defensive move checking.
proficiencyCriteria: Explain the role of interpreter, bytecode compilation, and CPython virtual machine execution pipeline.
Formulate and evaluate complex mathematical expressions adhering to Python operator precedence and associativity.
Construct efficient algorithms utilizing while and for loops with appropriate break, continue, and loop-else clauses.
Manipulate single and multidimensional lists with slicing, in-place sorting, and list comprehensions.
Design decoupled functions with explicit parameter contracts, handle local vs global scopes, and manage exceptions with try-except.
